scope: Public synthetic practice cases with disclosed reference judgments; not a hidden assessment set.
rubric: PASS means the statement respects the supplied evidence, denominator, speaker role, and distinction between observations and proposals. It does not certify that an underlying business practice is ethically justified.

cases.reason: The statement attributes a descriptive claim to management.

cases.text: October units were 2% below September; this contrast alone does not identify a price effect.
cases.reason: Description and causal identification remain separate.

cases.text: An analyst raised next-quarter discounts; the supplied excerpt contains no management decision.
cases.reason: The speaker and status of the proposal are preserved.

cases.text: Reported June use is 72 of the 100 enrolled panel members who answered in May.
cases.reason: The denominator and selection rule are explicit.

cases.text: The supplied call excerpt describes no randomized or untreated comparison.
cases.reason: The statement concerns the available evidence only.

cases.text: Management described a price change at this retailer; other firms need separate evidence.
cases.reason: The claim is restricted to its source and firm.

cases.text: The available figures do not establish whether consumers benefited.
cases.reason: No welfare measure or justified counterfactual has been supplied.

cases.text: A proposed discount pilot could compare contribution margin and customer complaints while retaining an accessible opt-out; no pilot outcome is claimed.
cases.reason: A conditional proposal is distinguished from an observed result.

cases.text: The 5% price increase caused the entire 2% fall in units.
cases.reason: The causal attribution exceeds a before-after comparison.

cases.text: Higher prices prove that customers are better off.
cases.reason: A price change establishes no consumer-welfare ranking.

cases.text: The analyst question confirms management will implement discounts.
cases.reason: An analyst question is not a management announcement.
The 100 selected respondents are not all customers.
